meta.notes: interpolate: 'from' and 'to' interpolated in 'space' with 'hue' at 'progress'. convert: 'from' converted to 'space' with missing components carried forward. Expected coordinates are in the units of the space (null = missing). The § 13.3 carry-forward examples give the colors 'to be interpolated', checked at progress 0 or 1. Each case has 'abs': half a unit of the last printed digit, unless a note says otherwise.

tolerance.rationale: Default for cases without 'abs': the examples print 3 decimals.

cases.note: The example converts the inputs to lab(66.927% 4.873 68.622) and lab(53.503% 82.672 -33.901); the conversion of the current CSS Color 4 sample code gives lab(53.504318 82.664556 -33.887015) for the second one, 0.014 away in b. The tolerance covers the difference of the stale intermediate values, not an error of the interpolation.
Same inputs as the Lab example (lch(53.5% 89.35 337.7) printed for the second color; the current conversion gives 89.3407 337.7096).

The first color converts to oklch(56.897% 0.0001 0) but its missing hue is carried forward and filled from the second color, oklch(63.612% 0.1522 78.748). Printed with 3 to 5 decimals (hue 78.748): tolerance half a unit of the coarsest printed digit.
The missing blue of the second color has no analog in OKLCh and becomes 0 in the conversion. Printed with 3 to 5 decimals (hue 78.748): tolerance half a unit of the coarsest printed digit.
